company.name: Stackwise
company.description: Project management for creative agencies: briefs, tasks and client approvals in one place, billed per seat.

title: Stackwise: trials that go nowhere
brief: Stackwise gets plenty of trial signups from agencies, but few become paying teams. The founder has a list of features competitors have, and support has a list of things that break every week. You have one sprint and a small team. Choose the work that turns trials into customers.

hidden.keyInsight: Of the 20 tickets, 4 are traps and 1 critical problem is filed as minor. The best sprint delivers 625 points of value with 9 tickets, using 32 of 34 story points.
hidden.principle: A sprint is a bet on outcomes. If a ticket cannot name the metric it moves, it is decoration.

stakeholders.name: Samir
priorities: Hit the growth number promised to the board
Have something impressive to show investors

stakeholders.name: Yuki
priorities: Close the deals in this quarter's pipeline
Never tell a prospect 'it is not on the roadmap'

stakeholders.name: Kofi
priorities: Fix what customers complain about every day

stakeholders.name: Viktor
priorities: Time to pay down tech debt

stakeholders.name: Chloe
priorities: More signups from the same traffic
A launch to talk about every month

tickets.title: Alerting on error rates and queue depth
tickets.description: Today the team learns about incidents from customer emails. Basic alerts would cut detection time from hours to minutes.

visible.impactHint: Last incident went unnoticed for 3 hours.

hidden.explanation: Every future incident gets shorter. High leverage for a few points.

tickets.title: Referral programme with rewards
tickets.description: Give users credit for every friend they bring. Referrals could double our signups.

hidden.explanation: It might work, but the claim has no baseline: nobody knows how many users refer today. A share link and a week of data would tell.

tickets.title: Rewrite the pricing page before the price change
tickets.description: New prices go live on the 1st. The current page still describes the old plans and would show wrong numbers at checkout.

visible.impactHint: The new prices go live either way.

hidden.explanation: Not every CEO request is a trap. This one has a fixed date and a concrete cost if it slips: customers shown the wrong price.

tickets.title: Turn down verbose request logging
tickets.description: Debug logging was left on after the last incident. Logs include full request headers and are shipped to our third-party log tool.

hidden.explanation: Full request headers contain customers' API keys and session tokens, now stored at a third party. It is a credential exposure filed as log hygiene.

tickets.title: AI assistant on the home screen
tickets.description: Every competitor announced an AI feature this quarter. We need a chat assistant on the home screen before the conference so there is something to demo.

visible.impactHint: The board asked what our AI story is.

hidden.explanation: Built for a demo, not for a user problem. No use case, no success metric, and a lot of cost and debt.

tickets.title: Fix the flaky test suite
tickets.description: One in three CI runs fails for no reason and is simply re-run. Engineers estimate half a day lost per person every week.

visible.impactHint: Roughly 10% of engineering time is lost to re-runs.

hidden.explanation: It moves no product metric, yet it hands back capacity in every future sprint. It pays for itself within two.

tickets.title: Invite teammates during signup
tickets.description: Accounts that add a second user in the first week almost never leave, but the invite option is buried in settings.

hidden.explanation: Puts the strongest known retention driver in front of every new account, at moderate cost.

tickets.title: Password reset emails arrive more than 10 minutes late
tickets.description: Reset emails sit in a low-priority queue behind marketing sends. Users request the email several times, then write to support or give up.

hidden.explanation: A cheap fix for one of the top support drivers. Users who cannot log in do not complain for long: they leave.

tickets.title: Let users choose which emails they receive
tickets.description: Today it is all or nothing. Users who find one notification noisy unsubscribe from everything, including the emails that bring them back.

hidden.explanation: Protects the re-engagement channel, but the effect is indirect and gradual. Worth doing when there is room.

tickets.title: Board dashboard with weekly KPIs
tickets.description: The CEO assembles the board numbers by hand from three tools every month. A dashboard would give them live.

hidden.explanation: Saves one person a couple of hours a month. Real but small, and no customer ever sees it.

tickets.title: Import from spreadsheets with column mapping
tickets.description: New customers arrive with their data in spreadsheets. The current import only accepts our own template, so onboarding calls are spent reformatting files.

visible.impactHint: Onboarding calls spend 40 minutes on manual import.

hidden.explanation: Every new account hits this wall on day one. High value, though it is a large piece of work.

tickets.title: Upgrading to a paid plan fails for about 1 in 5 attempts
tickets.description: Since the last release the upgrade button returns an error for some users. They are trying to pay and cannot.

hidden.explanation: Revenue is being turned away at the last step, every day. Nothing else in the backlog pays back as fast.

tickets.title: 4-4-5 fiscal calendar reporting for Halvorsen Group
tickets.description: Halvorsen Group closes its books on a 4-4-5 week calendar. They want every report and date filter to follow it.

visible.impactHint: Halvorsen Group's CFO raised it personally.

hidden.explanation: A calendar one account uses, threaded through every date in the product. An export they can regroup themselves is the proportionate answer.

tickets.title: Login loop on Safari since last Tuesday's release
tickets.description: Safari users are sent back to the login page after entering correct credentials. There is no workaround except switching browser.

hidden.explanation: A large group of users is locked out of the product by a regression. That is an incident, not a backlog item.

tickets.title: Activity log for account admins
tickets.description: Admins want to see who changed what and when. Security questionnaires from larger prospects ask for it explicitly.

hidden.explanation: A genuine requirement for larger accounts, but it only matters to a slice of the pipeline and it is not small.

tickets.title: Replace blank screens with helpful empty states
tickets.description: Seven screens show nothing at all until the user creates data. Each should explain what goes there and offer the next step.

hidden.explanation: Useful polish for first-time users, with a modest effect on its own.

tickets.title: Search: typo tolerance and recent items
tickets.description: Search only matches exact words. One in five queries returns nothing, and most of those are misspellings of things that exist.

hidden.explanation: A real, measured friction for regular users. Solid mid-value work, though not cheap.

tickets.title: Main menu covers the content on small phones
tickets.description: On screens narrower than 360px the menu stays open over the page. Users have to rotate the phone to reach the primary button.

hidden.explanation: Blocks a core action for a meaningful share of mobile users, and it is quick to fix.

tickets.title: Navigation is unusable on narrow screens
tickets.description: On the smallest phones the open menu sits on top of the page and hides the main button. Found during the last design review.

hidden.explanation: Same work as STK-350 ("Main menu covers the content on small phones"), described by a different team. Shipping both delivers the value once and pays for the effort twice.

tickets.title: Remove the legacy v1 API code
tickets.description: No client has called v1 since March, but its code paths still have to be kept compiling and tested.

hidden.explanation: Tidy and safe to do, but nothing gets worse if it waits another sprint.

midSprintEvents.title: Production incident: file uploads fail in every workspace
midSprintEvents.description: Since last night's deploy no customer can attach files. Ingrid traced it to an expired storage credential that was never rotated. Support has 60 tickets and counting.

addedTicket.title: Hotfix: rotate storage credentials and restore uploads
addedTicket.description: Rotate the credential, restore uploads and add the rotation to the release checklist so it cannot expire unnoticed again.

hidden.explanation: Production is broken for customers right now. Nothing planned before the incident is worth more than ending it.

hidden.guidance: An outage outranks planned work. Pull the hotfix in and take the lowest-value items out to make room: adding it on top of a full sprint only moves the failure to the end of the sprint.
